narrative.intro: Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C recorded $2.3B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C won 7 awards this fiscal year, yielding an average award size of $329M and driving obligations up 1171.7% year over year. Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C has concentrated obligations in the Department of Homeland Security, which obligated $2.2B, while the Department of Defense obligated $99M. Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C’s recent fiscal trajectory shows modest annual obligations from FY21 through FY25, with FY21 at $259M, FY22 at $168M, FY23 at $195M, FY24 at $54.5M, and FY25 at $181M. Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C’s current-year totals are partial, reflecting fiscal year to date figures rather than full-year results. Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C’s concentration of dollars in a single agency explains the large year-over-year increase in obligations for FY2026 to date. Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C should expect agency-level exposure to drive near-term revenue visibility given the current award and agency mix.

sections.heading: Who are the biggest buyers of Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security is the largest buyer, obligating $2.2B in FY2026 to date. The Department of Defense is the second buyer, obligating $99M. Agency concentration is high because those two agencies account for nearly all reported obligations this fiscal year.

sections.heading: How has Bollinger Shipyards Lockport L L C’s federal business changed recently?
sections.body: Obligations rose sharply, up 1171.7% year over year in FY2026 to date. Annual obligations were $259M in FY21, $168M in FY22, $195M in FY23, $54.5M in FY24, and $181M in FY25. The FY2026 to date total is $2.3B and represents partial-year results.
